title: Alaska Personal Care Assistance (PCA) / Community First Choice (CFC)
description: Alaska's Personal Care Assistance program and Community First Choice (1915k) option provide consumer-directed personal care services to Medicaid-eligible individuals with functional limitations. The PCA program is a state plan entitlement with no waitlist, and participants can hire family members including spouses as paid caregivers. Alaska's high pay rates reflect the elevated cost of living.
benefits_summary: Alaska PCA and CFC provide personal care assistance services including help with activities of daily living. Participants can hire family members, including spouses, as paid caregivers at approximate hourly rates of $16-$22/hr, reflecting Alaska's high cost of living. The PCA program is a state plan entitlement with no waitlist. CFC (1915k) provides additional self-direction options.

title: Alabama Personal Choices (Self-Directed Care)
description: Alabama Personal Choices is a self-directed care option available under the Elderly & Disabled Waiver and the State of Alabama Independent Living (SAIL) waiver. Participants can hire, manage, and supervise their own attendants, including family members and spouses, to provide personal care and home-based services as an alternative to agency-directed care.
benefits_summary: Alabama Personal Choices provides self-directed personal care services through HCBS waivers. Participants can hire family members, including spouses, as paid caregivers at approximate hourly rates of $10-$14/hr. Waitlists are typical for waiver enrollment. Services include assistance with activities of daily living, personal care, and homemaker tasks.

title: Arkansas IndependentChoices / ARChoices in Homecare
description: Arkansas IndependentChoices and ARChoices in Homecare provide consumer-directed personal care services through HCBS waivers and the 1915(j) Self-Directed Personal Assistance Services option. Arkansas was one of the original Cash & Counseling demonstration states. Family members can be hired as paid caregivers, but spouses are excluded from serving as paid attendants.
benefits_summary: ARChoices in Homecare provides home and community-based services for adults 21-64 with physical disabilities and seniors 65+. Services include Attendant Care (help with bathing, dressing, meals, toileting), Home-Delivered Meals, Personal Emergency Response Systems (PERS), Adult Day Services, Adult Day Health Services, Respite Care (facility-based and in-home), and Environmental Modifications (grab bars, wheelchair ramps). Family members (but not spouses) can be hired as paid attendant care workers at approximately $13-$15/hr. Income limit: 3x SSI standard ($2,742/month for 2023, updated annually). Resource limit: $2,000 for applicant. Individuals over the income limit may qualify by establishing an Income Trust. Must require Intermediate Level of Care as determined by the Office of Long Term Care. Arkansas was one of the original Cash & Counseling demonstration states.

verification.notes: Enriched from humanservices.arkansas.gov via Firecrawl. Income limit 3x SSI SPA ($2,742/mo for 2023). Resource limit $2,000. Application via access.arkansas.gov. Ages 21+ (21-64 with physical disability, 65+ any). Intermediate level of care required.

title: Arizona Self-Directed Attendant Care (AHCCCS/ALTCS)
description: Arizona Long Term Care System (ALTCS) is a managed care 1115 waiver that provides self-directed attendant care options. Participants can hire family members including spouses as paid caregivers. ALTCS is an entitlement program within Arizona's AHCCCS Medicaid system, so there is no formal waitlist, though the enrollment process can be lengthy.
benefits_summary: Arizona ALTCS provides self-directed attendant care through its managed care 1115 waiver. Participants can hire family members, including spouses, as paid caregivers at approximate hourly rates of $14-$18/hr. As an entitlement program, there is no formal waitlist, though enrollment processing can take time. Services include personal care, homemaker, and attendant care.

title: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) Program
description: The In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) program provides in-home assistance to eligible aged, blind, and disabled individuals as an alternative to out-of-home care, allowing recipients to remain safely in their own homes.
benefits_summary: Authorized services include housecleaning, meal preparation, laundry, grocery shopping, personal care services (such as bathing and grooming), paramedical services, accompaniment to medical appointments, and protective supervision for the mentally impaired. Recipients may receive up to 283 hours per month (average ~124 hours/month). The program pays providers (who can be family members) to perform these tasks, with the recipient acting as the employer. Provider wages vary by county.

verification.notes: Verified against cdss.ca.gov source; income limits tied to Medi-Cal (138% FPL); max 283 hrs/mo

title: California Paid Family Leave (PFL)
description: California's Paid Family Leave program provides up to 8 weeks of partial wage replacement benefits to workers who need time off to care for a seriously ill family member, bond with a new child, or participate in a qualifying military event. Funded entirely through employee payroll deductions via State Disability Insurance (SDI).
benefits_summary: Up to 8 weeks of wage replacement benefits in a 12-month period. Pays approximately 70-90% of wages (depending on income level) up to a maximum of $1,765 per week in 2026. Benefits are calculated based on wages earned 5 to 18 months before the claim start date. Leave can be taken all at once, intermittently, or on a reduced schedule. Note: PFL provides wage replacement only — it does not provide job protection (use CFRA or FMLA for that).

related_programs.note: FMLA provides job protection but no wage replacement; PFL provides wage replacement but no job protection

verification.notes: Verified against edd.ca.gov. 2026 max weekly benefit $1,765. 8 weeks duration. Funded by employee SDI deductions. No employer size requirement.

title: Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit (CDCTC)
description: Federal tax credit for expenses paid for the care of a qualifying child under age 13 or a disabled spouse or dependent of any age, to enable the taxpayer to work or look for work. Credit ranges from 20% to 35% of qualifying expenses based on adjusted gross income.
benefits_summary: Tax credit for work-related care expenses. Up to $3,000 in qualifying expenses for one dependent, or $6,000 for two or more dependents. Credit rate ranges from 20% to 35% of expenses based on AGI (35% for AGI up to $15,000, decreasing by 1% per $2,000 AGI to 20% for AGI over $43,000). Maximum credit: $1,050 for one qualifying person or $2,100 for two or more (at 35% rate). Non-refundable for tax year 2025. Qualifying persons include children under 13, disabled spouse, or disabled dependent of any age who is incapable of self-care. If spouse is full-time student or disabled, deemed earned income of $250/month (one qualifying person) or $500/month (two or more). Dependent care FSA benefits (max $5,000) reduce dollar limit for credit. Must file jointly if married (exceptions for legally separated or living apart last 6 months). Care provider cannot be spouse, parent of qualifying child under 13, or claimed dependent. Claimed via Form 2441.

verification.notes: Enriched from IRS Pub 503 (2025) and Form 2441 instructions via Firecrawl. TY2025 confirmed: $3,000/$6,000 expense limits, 20%-35% credit rates, non-refundable, qualifying relative income threshold $5,200, student/disabled spouse deemed income $250/$500/month. TY2026 rates not yet published.

title: CHAMPVA (Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs)
description: Healthcare coverage program for spouses, surviving spouses, and dependent children of veterans who are permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, or who died from a service-connected condition. A cost-sharing program that covers inpatient, outpatient, mental health, pharmacy, and durable medical equipment.
benefits_summary: Cost-sharing healthcare coverage for eligible dependents and survivors of permanently and totally disabled or deceased Veterans. Covers: inpatient hospital care, outpatient medical visits, mental health services (preauthorization required), prescription medications (via OptumRx), durable medical equipment (DME), preventive care, ambulance services, and adjunctive dental (preauthorization required). Organ/bone marrow transplants require preauthorization. CHAMPVA is a cost-sharing program where VA shares the cost of covered services. Not available to those eligible for TRICARE. Surviving spouses who remarry at age 55+ retain eligibility. Dependent children covered until 18, or up to 23 if enrolled in school, or any age if permanently disabled before 18. If eligible for Medicare (age 65+), must have Medicare Parts A and B to keep CHAMPVA. Primary family caregivers may qualify via PCAFC. Apply online (VA Form 10-10d), by mail, or by fax to 303-331-7809. Contact: 800-733-8387 (Mon-Fri 8am-7:30pm ET).

related_programs.note: Primary family caregivers of veterans may receive CHAMPVA through PCAFC

verification.notes: Enriched from va.gov/family-and-caregiver-benefits/health-and-disability/champva/ and va.gov/COMMUNITYCARE/providers/info-champva.asp via Firecrawl. Confirmed: no income/asset test, 100% P&T disability or death from service-connected condition, dependent children under 18 (23 if in school, any age if helpless child), surviving spouse remarriage at 55+ retains, Medicare A+B required if 65+, preauthorization for dental/mental health/transplants, apply via Form 10-10d. title: Colorado Consumer Directed Attendant Support Services (CDASS)
description: Colorado Consumer Directed Attendant Support Services (CDASS) provides participants with a monthly budget to hire and manage their own attendants, including family members and spouses. Colorado implemented Community First Choice (1915k) with self-direction options. CDASS is available under multiple waivers including the Elderly Blind and Disabled (EBD) waiver.
benefits_summary: Colorado Consumer-Directed Attendant Support Services (CDASS) gives participants a monthly budget to hire, train, and manage their own attendants, including family members, friends, and spouses (with some restrictions), at approximate hourly rates of $15-$20/hr. As of July 1, 2025, CDASS is available only through the Community First Choice (CFC) program for Health Maintenance Activities (HMA), Homemaker, and Personal Care services. Participants must be enrolled in Health First Colorado (Colorado Medicaid) and meet CFC eligibility including institutional level of care. Current HCBS waiver members may continue under their waiver temporarily until their next Continued Stay Review. A Financial Management Services (FMS) provider (Consumer Direct Colorado) assists with budget management. No waitlist as a state plan entitlement. Apply via local Case Management Agency (CMA) or Health First Colorado enrollment at hcpf.colorado.gov/how-to-apply.

verification.notes: Enriched from hcpf.colorado.gov/consumer-directed-attendant-support-services via Firecrawl. Confirmed: CDASS transitioned to CFC as of July 1, 2025 for HMA, Homemaker, and Personal Care. Must be enrolled in Health First Colorado (Medicaid) and meet CFC eligibility (institutional level of care). Apply via local CMA or hcpf.colorado.gov/how-to-apply. FMS provider is Consumer Direct Colorado.

title: Colorado Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI)
description: Colorado's FAMLI program provides paid family and medical leave to nearly all Colorado workers. Employees can take up to 12 weeks of paid leave for family or medical reasons (up to 16 weeks with pregnancy complications). Jointly funded by employer and employee payroll premiums.
benefits_summary: Up to 12 weeks of paid family or medical leave per year, with an additional 4 weeks available for pregnancy or childbirth complications (16 weeks total). Uses a progressive wage replacement formula: 90% of wages up to 50% of the state average weekly wage (SAWW), plus 50% of wages above that threshold, with a maximum weekly benefit of $1,381.45 in 2026 (based on SAWW of $1,534.94). Includes job protection — employers must restore the employee to the same or equivalent position. Both employers and employees contribute through payroll premiums (0.9% of wages, split).

related_programs.note: CO FAMLI can run concurrently with FMLA leave

verification.notes: Verified against famli.colorado.gov. 2026 max weekly benefit $1,381.45 based on SAWW of $1,534.94. 12 weeks standard + 4 weeks pregnancy complications. Employer + employee funded at 0.9% of wages.

title: Connecticut Paid Family and Medical Leave (CT Paid Leave)
description: Connecticut's Paid Family and Medical Leave Act (PFMLA) provides paid, job-protected time off for eligible workers to care for a family member with a serious health condition, bond with a new child, serve as an organ or bone marrow donor, address needs related to military deployment, or manage their own serious health condition. Funded through employee payroll deductions.
benefits_summary: Up to 12 weeks of paid, job-protected leave per year (plus an additional 2 weeks for pregnancy-related incapacity). Benefit calculation: 95% of average weekly wage up to 40x CT minimum wage ($677.60 in 2026), plus 60% of wages above that threshold, capped at 60x CT minimum wage ($1,016.40 per week in 2026). Funded entirely through employee payroll deductions (0.5% of wages). Includes job protection — employers must restore the employee to the same or equivalent position.

related_programs.note: CT Paid Leave can run concurrently with FMLA leave

title: DC Elderly and Persons with Physical Disabilities Waiver (Self-Direction)

Family members can be hired as attendants, though spouses are excluded. DC also offers an Individual and Family Support (IFS) waiver for individuals with intellectual disabilities with additional self-direction options.

DC also has the IFS waiver for individuals with intellectual disabilities.

title: District of Columbia Universal Paid Leave (UPL)
description: DC's Universal Paid Leave program provides up to 12 weeks of partial wage replacement for workers who need time off to care for a seriously ill family member, bond with a new child, or recover from their own serious health condition. Benefits have been available since July 1, 2020. The program uses a sliding-scale formula: 90% of the first $900/week of wages plus 50% of wages above that threshold, up to a maximum of $1,190/week. Fully employer-funded through a 0.75% payroll tax. Notably, DC UPL does NOT provide job protection, unlike most state paid family leave programs.
benefits_summary: Up to 12 weeks of wage replacement for family caregiving, 12 weeks for parental bonding, 12 weeks for own medical leave, and 2 weeks for prenatal leave. Sliding-scale formula: 90% of the first ~$900/week of wages plus 50% of wages above that, up to a maximum of $1,190/week (effective September 28, 2025). Covered family members include spouse, domestic partner, parent, parent-in-law, child, grandparent, and sibling. Funded entirely by employer payroll tax at 0.75% of wages. Does NOT provide job protection (unlike most other state PFML programs).

related_programs.note: FMLA provides federal job protection for eligible employees; DC UPL provides wage replacement but no job protection

verification.notes: Enriched from dcpaidfamilyleave.dc.gov/workers/ via Firecrawl. Confirmed: 12 weeks each for family, medical, and parental leave plus 2 weeks prenatal. Max weekly benefit $1,190 (effective Sept 28, 2025; site still shows $1,153 pre-update). Must be currently employed (not receiving unemployment). Private sector only - excludes DC govt, federal, WMATA, religious institutions. Self-employed may opt in. Application URL confirmed. Employer-funded via 0.75% payroll tax. No job protection.

title: Delaware Paid Family and Medical Leave (Healthy Delaware Families Act)
description: Delaware's Paid Family and Medical Leave program, created by the Healthy Delaware Families Act, provides paid, job-protected leave for eligible workers to bond with a new child, care for a family member with a serious health condition, manage their own serious health condition, or address military exigencies. Benefits launched January 1, 2026. Employer-funded with optional employee cost-sharing.

Pays 80% of the employee's average weekly wage, up to a maximum of $900 per week in 2026. Employers with 10-24 employees are required to provide parental leave only; employers with 25+ employees must provide the full program. Includes job protection.

title: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
description: Refundable federal tax credit for low-to-moderate income working individuals and families. The credit amount depends on earned income, filing status, and number of qualifying children. Designed to supplement wages and reduce poverty for working families.
benefits_summary: Refundable tax credit for working individuals and families. Tax year 2025 maximum credits: $649 (no children), $4,328 (1 child), $7,152 (2 children), $8,046 (3+ children). AGI limits for single/head of household: $19,104 (no children) to $61,555 (3+ children). For married filing jointly: $26,214 (no children) to $68,675 (3+ children). Investment income must be $11,950 or less. Tax year 2026: max credit increases to $8,231 for 3+ children. Must have earned income and valid SSN.

title: Florida Alzheimer's Disease Initiative (ADI)
description: The Florida Alzheimer's Disease Initiative (ADI), administered by the Florida Department of Elder Affairs (DOEA) through Area Agencies on Aging, provides support services specifically for family caregivers of individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementia disorders. Services include in-home respite care, caregiver training and education, case management, support groups, supplemental supplies (incontinence products, nutritional supplements), adult day care, and emergency respite. The program targets moderate-to-low income families who cannot afford private dementia care.
benefits_summary: ADI provides family caregivers of Alzheimer's and dementia patients with respite care (in-home and adult day), caregiver training (including behavioral management techniques), individual and group counseling, case management, and supplemental supplies such as incontinence products and nutritional supplements. Services are coordinated through local Area Agencies on Aging and Aging Service Networks. Sliding scale fees apply; no caregiver is turned away for inability to pay. Eligibility requires care recipient to have a confirmed or suspected Alzheimer's or related dementia diagnosis.

verification.notes: Florida ADI administered by DOEA through AAAs. State-funded caregiver support program specifically for dementia caregivers. Sliding scale fees; no hard income cutoff. Care recipient must have Alzheimer's or related dementia. Program availability varies by county.

title: Florida Statewide Medicaid Managed Care - Participant Directed Option (PDO)
description: Florida's Participant Directed Option (PDO) within the Statewide Medicaid Managed Care Long-Term Care program allows enrollees to hire family members including spouses and legally responsible individuals as paid caregivers. Eight managed care plans offer PDOs, with each plan setting its own fee schedule. As of June 2020, approximately 7,841 participants used PDO out of roughly 51,848 HCBS enrollees. Florida also has CDC+ for developmental disabilities.
benefits_summary: Florida PDO provides participant-directed personal care through managed care. Participants can hire family members, including spouses and legally responsible individuals, as paid caregivers at approximate hourly rates of $12-$16/hr (varies by managed care plan). Waitlists are typical for waiver enrollment. No licensing is required for personal care, homemaker, or companion services. Eight managed care plans offer PDOs with each setting its own fee schedule.

title: Florida Community Care for the Elderly (CCE)
description: The Florida Community Care for the Elderly (CCE) program, administered by the Florida Department of Elder Affairs (DOEA) through Area Agencies on Aging and Lead Agencies, provides community-based services to help functionally impaired older adults (60+) remain in their own homes and avoid institutionalization. Services directly support family caregivers by providing in-home assistance including homemaker services, personal care, home-delivered meals, transportation, adult day care, and case management. Funded through state appropriations and OAA.
benefits_summary: CCE delivers in-home and community services that keep older adults at home and relieve caregiver burden. Services include homemaker assistance (cleaning, laundry, meal preparation), personal care (bathing, grooming), home-delivered meals, transportation, adult day care, case management, and emergency alert systems. Eligibility requires care recipient to be 60+ with a functional impairment that places them at risk of nursing home placement. Sliding scale cost-sharing; lowest-income clients pay nothing. Services are accessed through local Area Agencies on Aging by calling Elder Helpline: 1-800-963-5337.

verification.notes: Florida CCE program administered by DOEA through AAAs and Lead Agencies. State-funded; care recipient must be 60+ with functional impairment at risk of institutionalization. No hard income cutoff; sliding scale. Elder Helpline 1-800-963-5337 to apply.

title: FMLA Military Caregiver Leave
description: Extension of FMLA providing up to 26 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a single 12-month period for an eligible employee to care for a covered servicemember or veteran with a serious injury or illness.
benefits_summary: Up to 26 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a single 12-month period to care for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness. This is inclusive of the standard 12 weeks of FMLA leave. Covered servicemembers include current Armed Forces members (including National Guard and Reserves) and veterans discharged within the preceding 5 years. Covered relationships include spouse, son, daughter, parent, or next of kin (nearest blood relative).

related_programs.note: Extends standard FMLA eligibility requirements and protections

title: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
description: Federal law requiring covered employers to provide up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year for qualifying family and medical reasons, including caring for a spouse, child, or parent with a serious health condition.
benefits_summary: Up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period. Employer must maintain group health insurance during leave. Employee must be restored to same or equivalent position upon return. Qualifying reasons include: caring for spouse, child, or parent with serious health condition; employee's own serious health condition; birth/adoption of child.

title: Medicaid HCBS Waivers (Home and Community-Based Services)
description: Federal Medicaid waiver program under Section 1915(c) allowing states to provide home and community-based services as an alternative to institutional care. Services include respite care, personal care assistance, adult day health, home modifications, and more. States design their own waivers within federal guidelines.
benefits_summary: Home and community-based services as alternative to nursing home placement. Services vary by state but typically include: personal care/attendant services, respite care, adult day health, home modifications, assistive technology, case management, and skilled nursing. As of 2025: 259 active 1915(c) waivers in 47 states + DC, 15 states with 1115 HCBS waivers, 10 states with 1915(k) Community First Choice. Over 5.1 million people receive Medicaid home care annually. All 50 responding states pay family caregivers through at least one program. 49 states (all except Alaska) allow self-direction. 44 states allow payment to legally responsible relatives via waiver. Family caregiver payments range $10-$22/hour depending on state. 11 states offer structured family caregiving programs ($40-70/day). Waitlists are common. See data/inventory/hcbs-waivers-by-state.json for the complete state-by-state waiver inventory.

related_programs.note: Must be Medicaid-eligible or meet institutional level of care

title: SSDI (Social Security Disability Insurance)
description: Federal insurance program providing monthly cash benefits to workers who become disabled and can no longer perform substantial gainful activity. Based on work history and payroll tax contributions, not income-tested.
benefits_summary: Monthly cash benefit based on lifetime average earnings. Average SSDI payment approximately $1,630/month in 2026 (2.8% COLA). Maximum benefit varies by work history. Generally 40 credits needed (20 in last 10 years), younger workers may qualify with fewer. 5-month waiting period before benefits begin. At full retirement age, SSDI converts to retirement benefits at same amount.

title: Texas Community First Choice (CFC) / Consumer Directed Services (CDS)
description: Texas Community First Choice (CFC) is a 1915(k) Medicaid state plan option (since 2015) providing personal assistance services to individuals with functional limitations. Consumer Directed Services (CDS) is an option within multiple HCBS waivers (STAR+PLUS, CLASS, DBMD, HCS) allowing participants to hire, manage, and supervise their own attendants, including family members and spouses, as an alternative to agency-directed care.
benefits_summary: CFC and CDS provide personal assistance services including help with activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, grooming, eating), health maintenance tasks, and habilitation services. CFC was established by SB 7 (2013 Legislature) and began June 1, 2015. Under CDS, the participant (or their legally authorized representative) serves as the employer of record, hiring and managing their own attendants. Family members, including spouses, can be hired as paid caregivers. Hourly pay rates range from $10-$18/hr depending on the managed care organization and geographic region. CFC is available as an entitlement to Medicaid-eligible individuals who need help with ADLs and meet institutional (nursing facility) level of care criteria. States receive 6% increase in federal matching funds for CFC services. HCBS waiver-based CDS options (STAR+PLUS, CLASS, DBMD, HCS) often have long waitlists, particularly for IDD waivers which can have multi-year waits. Individuals on 1915(c) waiver interest lists who meet eligibility requirements may be eligible for CFC services.

title: Texas Lifespan Respite Care Program
description: The Texas Lifespan Respite Care Program provides temporary relief (respite) to family and informal caregivers of individuals of all ages with disabilities, special health care needs, or chronic conditions. Administered by the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) through a statewide network of Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) and local provider organizations. Funded through OAA Title III-E, MIECHV, and Texas state appropriations. Caregivers of older adults, children with special health care needs, adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities, and individuals with physical disabilities are all served.
benefits_summary: Provides temporary respite care to give family caregivers a break from their caregiving duties. Services include in-home respite, adult day services, overnight respite, emergency respite, and caregiver training. Serves caregivers of individuals of all ages with disabilities or special needs — children with special health care needs, adults with intellectual/developmental disabilities, older adults, and adults with physical disabilities or chronic conditions. No income requirement; services prioritized by assessed need and local provider capacity. Contact your local Area Agency on Aging or call 2-1-1 Texas to find local respite services.

verification.notes: Texas Lifespan Respite Care Program administered by HHSC through AAAs. Funded via OAA Title III-E and state appropriations. No income test; eligibility based on caregiver need and care recipient disability/special need. Services vary by local provider.

title: Texas STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Waiver
description: The Texas STAR+PLUS HCBS waiver (1915(c)) provides home and community-based services to Medicaid-eligible adults 21 and older who have physical disabilities or are age 65+ and require a nursing facility level of care. Unlike the CFC entitlement program, STAR+PLUS HCBS provides an expanded service array including personal attendant care, home health, adult day health, day activity and health services, supported employment, financial management services, and emergency response. The Consumer Directed Services (CDS) option allows family members to be hired as paid attendants. Administered by managed care organizations under HHSC.
benefits_summary: STAR+PLUS HCBS provides an extended service array beyond basic personal care: adult day health care, home health aide, nursing, respite (up to 35 days/year for live-in caregivers), supported employment, day activity and health services (DAHS), and financial management. Under the CDS option, participants can hire and manage their own attendants, including family members. Pays attendants $10–$18/hr depending on managed care organization. Waitlists are common; apply as early as possible. Medicaid eligibility (income ~138% FPL) and nursing-facility level of care required.

related_programs.note: CDS is the self-direction option within STAR+PLUS; CFC (tx-consumer-directed) is a separate entitlement

title: Vermont Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FMLI)
description: Vermont's Family and Medical Leave Insurance plan is a VOLUNTARY, insurance-based paid family leave program — NOT a mandatory universal payroll-tax program like most other state PFML laws. Mandatory for state employees only; private employers may opt in voluntarily through phased expansion: Phase 1 (July 2023) state employees, Phase 2 (July 2024) employers with 2+ employees, Phase 3 (July 2025) all employers including 1 employee and self-employed. Provides up to 6 weeks of wage replacement at approximately 60% of average weekly wages, up to roughly $1,074/week. Administered through The Hartford insurance company. Does NOT provide job protection.
benefits_summary: VOLUNTARY opt-in program (not mandatory for private employers). Up to 6 weeks of wage replacement at approximately 60% of average weekly wages, up to roughly $1,074/week. Covers care for a seriously ill family member (spouse, parent, child, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, parent-in-law), bonding with a new child, and own medical leave. Mandatory for state employees; voluntary for private employers through phased expansion: Phase 2 (July 2024) opened to employers with 2+ employees; Phase 3 (July 2025) opened to all employers and self-employed. title: Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML)
description: Washington State's Paid Family and Medical Leave program provides paid time off for workers who need to care for a family member with a serious health condition, bond with a new child, or address certain military-connected events.
